findings.desc: packages/main/src/cli/help-renderer.ts:52 BRIEF_DESC_MAX=10 truncates every per-command description in brief help to 10 CHARACTERS (not words), producing useless fragments like "List Proo…", "Report ov…", "Advance a…", "Probe one…" for essentially all ~320 commands. Live repro: node bin/lattice.js help shows host_probe  Probe one… and host_status  Report ov… — indistinguishable, no actual information about what each command does. This directly violates the CHK-003 adversarial acceptance intent brief must not degrade agent decision-making for the help catalog: an agent cannot pick the right command from these fragments and must always fall back to --full, defeating the token-savings goal of the story. brief-output-smoke.ts:256-265 only asserts byte-budget and branding presence, never asserts description content is meaningful, so this shipped undetected. Likely a units bug (10 chars vs intended ~40-60 chars or 10 words) given the surrounding budget reasoning in the code comment. Severity high because it materially breaks CHK-003s stated purpose while still passing all recorded evidence.

packages/main/src/handlers/story-query.ts:654 (openBugStories filter) changes story_list dashboard-summary CONTENT, not just rendering verbosity: it adds a DISCARDED exclusion to the not-closed bug-story flag, present in BOTH brief and --full output. This is a genuine logic/behavior fix (re-applying a regression of commit 288d359377 fix: ignore discarded bug stories in story_list from Apr 2026, which had been lost from the codebase before this story started per git show ac83c67618^). The story background/plan.md frames this story as rendering-only output hygiene with gate/state-machine behavior changes explicitly out of scope, and this specific fix is not named in plan.md CHK-004 or the scope-contract scopeChangeReason. It is well-evidenced (CHK-005:edge:1 runs scripts/verify-story-list-bug-summary.mjs green) and appears correct/desirable, but it is an undeclared drive-by content change riding on a story whose stated boundary is rendering-only; the code comment mischaracterizes it as accommodating a pre-existing test rather than restoring lost behavior. Severity low/advisory: functionally correct and tested, but a precedent worth flagging for scope discipline.

CHK-004:edge:1 (should): host_list borderline case (15,899 bytes, confirmed live) has no verificationEvidence record bound to this intentRef and no explicit disposition in docs/CLI.md. The CHK-004:edge:0 sweep evidence note lists host_list in an inline audited-under-threshold list ("host_list 15,899"), but the intent explicitly requires the borderline case be EITHER brought under brief-by-default OR explicitly documented as acceptable — docs/CLI.md brief-outputs table omits host_list entirely (unlike story_get, which gets a dedicated audited-disposition paragraph). So the disposition exists only in an evidence-log free-text note, not in the doc surface the intent points to, and is not bound to CHK-004:edge:1.

CHK-001:edge:1 and CHK-003:edge:1 (both should-priority scaling boundaries) lack any verificationEvidence: milestone_status with >20 milestones, and help with >100 registered commands. brief-output-smoke.ts fixtures only build 3 milestones (msBrief asserts "3 total" at line 209) and the live help catalog already has ~320 commands (well over 100) but no test asserts the brief renderer stays one-line-per-milestone / grouped-and-readable at that scale without truncation loss of identifiers. No evidence record exists for either intentRef.
